summary: crypto-javas exfiltrates CI/CD environment variables at install and import
details: The package typosquats crypto-js and ships credential-harvest code with no cryptographic functionality. package.json declares a postinstall hook (`node setup.js`) that enumerates process.env, excludes only a short list of non-sensitive OS vars, and POSTs every remaining variable (tokens, cloud keys, deploy credentials) plus CI job identifiers (CI_JOB_ID, GITHUB_SHA, project, branch, hostname) to a backend URL loaded from BACKEND_URL/BACKEND_API_KEY (env, a `js-crypto` section in package.json,.crypto-config.json, or.env). The main module additionally runs `autoExecute()` at top level on require/import, instantiating SecretsHandler, reading environment variables, and calling sendToBackend, so environment exfiltration also fires for any consumer that imports the package even with `npm install --ignore-scripts`. Repository URL is a placeholder (gitlab.com/example/js-crypto.git) and author is a generic `DevSecOps` string.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
